# A dock tab reorder desyncs its header from the committed document

## Context

Found while grounding the DockLayouts mechanics guide with real pointer gestures on `examples/dashboard/dock` at `dev@cce07cdade`, reading each gesture on three planes: the DOM, the committed document through `Neo.worker.App.getConfigs`, and the live instances through the Neural Link on a headless session of my own. The observed operation is an ordinary within-toolbar tab drag, followed by tab clicks and a cross-zone tab drag in the same header.

Reproduction, one fresh page per arm (bridge disabled, 1.5–2.5 s idle after every gesture, no console error in either arm):

| Step | Arm A: header shows | Arm A: committed | Arm B (control, no reorder): committed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Boot | Strategy · Swarm · Metrics · Timeline · … | same order, `activeItemId: strategy` | same |
| Drag Swarm behind Timeline | Strategy · Timeline · Swarm · Metrics · …, live active index 3 — the button reading Metrics | strategy · metrics · timeline · swarm · …, `activeItemId: swarm` | — |
| Click Metrics | no change: index 3 was already live-active | `activeItemId` stays `swarm` | `activeItemId: metrics` |
| Drag Metrics into Logs | Logs header: Logs · Metrics | `tabs-logs`: logs · swarm | `tabs-logs`: logs · metrics, and the header agrees |

Observed on the standalone example only; the classes involved are shared by every dock consumer, and the Workstation was not reproduced separately.

Not checked: whether any shipped consumer has already persisted a diverged document.

## The Problem

After a within-toolbar reorder, the header's live order and its reconciled `dockItemIds` stop describing the same items, and every later positional read resolves the wrong one:

- **The header selects a different tab than the document.** A move activates the moved item: after Swarm is dragged, the committed `activeItemId` is `swarm`, while the header's live active index sits on the button that reads "Metrics" — so clicking "Metrics" commits nothing. A click on a tab that is not live-active commits the item that used to hold its index: on the component tier at `dev@f9709716ad`, clicking "Timeline" after the same reorder committed `metrics`.
- **A drag moves a different item in the document and the dragged one on screen.** Dragging "Metrics" into the Logs zone committed `swarm` into `tabs-logs`, while the retained chrome moved the Metrics button and pane there; on the component tier, dragging "Timeline" committed `metrics`.
- **A second reorder moves a different item, even with the header's ids kept in step.** On the unit tier with only the `moveTo` override below applied, moving Beta to the end and then Delta to the front committed `[gamma, alpha, delta, beta]` — Gamma moved, not Delta.
- **The drift outlives the session.** Anything that writes the committed document — a saved perspective, *Save Current*, a Group snapshot — stores the diverged arrangement, and the next fresh projection shows the user a layout they never built.

Live-instance receipt from that session, after the reorder, one click and one cross-zone drag (`query_component`, session `5b1d0386`): the main header's "Timeline" button carries `dockItemId: 'metrics'`; the Logs header's "Metrics" button carries `dockItemId: 'swarm'`, duplicating the Swarm button's own stamp; no button carries `'timeline'`. The committed document at that moment: `main-tabs` `[strategy, metrics, timeline, agents, alerts, history]`, `tabs-logs` `[logs, swarm]`.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/draggable/tab/header/toolbar/SortZone.mjs` `moveTo` calls `Neo.tab.Container#moveTo` (`src/tab/Container.mjs`), which reorders the **live** tab buttons and cards, then fires `moveTo`.
- The `LayoutAdapter` `moveTo` listener (`src/dashboard/dock/projection/LayoutAdapter.mjs`, the within-container reorder listener) commits `addTab {itemId: items[fromIndex], tabsNodeId, index: toIndex}`. For an item already in the tree `addTab` dispatches as `moveItem`, which re-enters `Operations.addTab` — and that sets the node's `activeItemId` to the moved item.
- `addTab` is change class `topology` (`model/Operations.mjs` `operationChangeClass`), so the projection runs the full reconciliation. `Reconciler.reconcileTabChrome` builds `liveItems` by zipping `bar.sortZoneConfig.dockItemIds[index]` — still in projection-time order, because the live move never touched it — with `body.items[index]`, which the live move already reordered. Each moved card is attributed to the item that used to occupy its index.
- Placement then follows the document using those attributions: a non-adjacent move lands its permutation twice, and an adjacent swap snaps back on screen while the document keeps the swap. The final pass writes `dockItemIds = desiredItems` and sets each button's text from the misattributed pane, so text and card agree with each other and disagree with `dockItemIds`.
- The listener's `items` is a second copy of the same identity: the node's item list captured when the projection built the container. `Reconciler.moveRetainedTabChrome` re-applies `listeners` only to retained chrome that changes parent; a container reconciled in place keeps its projection-time listener, so once one reorder has landed, the next resolves its item from the old order.
- Every consumer of the invariant "`dockItemIds[i]` names the item at live index `i`" inherits the error: `Workspace#getActiveDockItemId` (a tab click's `setActiveItem`), `TabSortZone`'s `dockItemIds[startIndex]` (a drag's item id and its drag-start `dockItemId` restamp), `reconcileTabChrome`'s `liveItems`, and the dock `TabContainer#presentDockLock`.
- Prior art: #15517 moved header focus identity from a positional index to the `dockItemId` stamp and named "manual reorder" as the case a positional map mis-handles with no alarm. This is the same class, one site over.

## The Fix

Keep one identity source, at the one mutation path that breaks it. `Neo.dashboard.dock.interaction.TabContainer` — the container a dock tabs node already projects into — overrides `moveTo(fromIndex, toIndex)` to move the id inside its tab bar's `sortZoneConfig.dockItemIds`, and the live sort zone's `dockItemIds`, before the `super` call. The `LayoutAdapter` `moveTo` listener reads the moved id from that live header — `dockItemIds[toIndex]` on the firing container — instead of its projection-time `items`. Positional readers are then aligned before the commit's projection lands and after it, `reconcileTabChrome` zips ids and cards that already agree, and `Neo.tab.Container` stays untouched.

## Decision Record impact

aligned-with ADR 0029 — the component-identity handoff the projection already promises.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Unit, red-first on `dev`: after a dock tabs node reorders through its container's `moveTo`, `sortZoneConfig.dockItemIds` matches the live buttons and cards immediately; after the committed `addTab` reconciles, every card, button text and `dockItemIds[i]` name the same item. Both shapes: a non-adjacent move and an adjacent swap.
- [ ] Unit: a second reorder, made after the first one's projection landed, commits the move of the item its button shows.
- [ ] Component tier, real pointer: reorder a tab within its header, then click a different tab — the committed `activeItemId` is the clicked item; then drag that tab to another zone — the committed document moves the dragged item, and its pane arrives as the same DOM node.
- [ ] The existing dock unit and component suites stay green.

## Out of Scope

- Any reorder path other than the header sort zone's `moveTo`; one found later is its own leaf.
- The Brain-gated whitebox reorder witness.

## Avoided Traps

- **Re-projecting the header from scratch after a reorder.** It would hide the drift by destroying the pane and chrome identity the reconciler exists to preserve.
- **Keying `liveItems` by the button's `dockItemId` stamp instead.** It fixes the reconcile but leaves every positional reader wrong until the projection lands, and it rests on a stamp that drag start rewrites from the positional ids.
- **Re-applying `listeners` on every in-place reconcile.** It would refresh the closure's order and keep the second copy of identity for the next mutation to stale.
- **A witness that asserts only the committed document.** The existing reorder arm does exactly that; the document is correct at the reorder itself, so it cannot see the divergence.
